overview.about: World Environment Day is the United Nations' flagship day for encouraging worldwide awareness and action for the environment. Led by the UN Environment Programme since 1974, it is marked in more than 150 countries and each year is hosted by a different nation around a set theme.
overview.nextEvent: The next World Environment Day is marked on 5 June, with a global host country and theme set by UN Environment. Governments, businesses and communities run campaigns and projects to tackle pressing environmental issues.

@graph.name: World Environment Day
@graph.description: World Environment Day is the United Nations’ main annual platform for public environmental action. Led by the United Nations Environment Programme and observed on 5 June, it gives each edition a theme and a host country while inviting local organisations to turn that focus into practical work. The day has covered issues from restoration and pollution to water, land and climate pressure. It works best as a starting point for a local decision: join a verified restoration activity, learn how a nearby ecosystem is managed, or follow the official campaign material to understand the year’s theme. UNEP is headquartered in Nairobi, which makes Kenya a useful place link for an observance that is global in reach.

exploreIntro: These examples show why World Environment Day is global rather than tied to one venue: Australia connects land and sea, Kenya connects biodiversity and livelihoods, and Switzerland connects Alpine water with climate.
participationIntro: Use the day for a concrete environmental action:

participationSteps.text: Choose a local issue to focus on: waste, water, air, biodiversity, food, transport or energy.
Take part in a community activity, workplace initiative or school action if one is available.
Share a practical environmental step that people can repeat after the day.
Keep claims specific and sourced; do not turn the day into generic green messaging.
